tasks.title: Prove supported solver and workspace parity
tasks.goal: Close candidate and configuration behavior across actually supported backends.
steps: Run the accepted feature/group corpus against each supported backend capability set.
Compare selected request/effect graph or equivalent typed conflict, including multi-member roots and capability/OR providers.
Keep unsupported semantics explicit and ensure all supported routes expose rejected-candidate reasons.
positive_cases: Each supported backend preserves all consumers and finds the same valid configuration class.
negative_cases: Candidate leakage, wrong-version conditional satisfaction and hidden fallback fail the corpus.

tasks.title: Close transaction and Redbook coexistence regressions
tasks.goal: Verify failure recovery, independent WAL/MUP use and current version policy.
steps: Inject failures before/after owned manifest, lock, slots, boot and hook prefixes.
Exercise independent WAL/MUP roots together, then Redbook exclusive selection in the same fixture matrix.
Check offline replay, shared-dependency retention, explicit missing-input behavior and no automatic Redbook bump.
positive_cases: Independent WAL/MUP coexist; Redbook contributes one selected branch.
Recovered transaction matches exact requested graph or reports partial effects.
negative_cases: Source corruption, concurrent edits or unsupported rollback never yield successful complete apply.
Group exclusivity cannot become a global package ban.
